summary.headline: Advit Jewels Q2 FY27 revenue rose about 24% YoY to INR59.1 crore, with net profit up 28% to INR12.76 crore and a 27.8% EBITDA margin.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue grew 23.93% YoY to INR59.1 crore, EBITDA rose 18.8% to INR16.4 crore at a 27.8% margin, and net profit grew 28% to INR12.76 crore (21.6% margin, up 68 bps). For H1, revenue grew 28.6% to INR94.5 crore, EBITDA margin was 29.8%, and net profit rose 31.7% to INR20.95 crore. Management attributed the EBITDA margin dip versus last year to higher marketing and exhibition spend ahead of B2C retail. Inventory rose INR27.7 crore since March 2026 to INR169 crore, mostly finished goods, to support the upcoming stores; the company says it is debt-free after repaying short-term bank debt from IPO proceeds.

financial_highlights.change: +18.8% YoY; margin down vs ~29% last year (per analyst)
INR27.7 crore rise in Q2 vs March 2026 (as stated)
Under concessional manufacturing tax regime per management

segments.name: B2B
segments.commentary: Management says the current mix is about 80:20 B2B to B2C. B2B remains the core channel in H1, which management describes as a lighter season.

segments.name: B2C / retail
segments.commentary: Company-owned Delhi Defence Colony store is targeted for Q4 (calendar 2027 per the call, ambiguous) and the 35,000 sq ft Jaipur flagship is under interior work. Target is about 30% B2C and 70% B2B next year.

guidance_outlook: Target B2C mix of about 30% and B2B about 70% next year, after the stores open.
Delhi Defence Colony store targeted to open in Q4; management said it may launch 'by Q4 for sure'.
Management expects B2C margins to be higher than B2B but declined to quantify a margin target.
Management says B2C expense has been incurred but B2C revenue will show mainly next year.
Plans to expand the business network across India, launch new collections, and expand internationally over time; no quantified growth target given.
capex_capacity: Integrated Jaipur facility with installed annual capacity of 400 kg of jewelry, with 3D printing and modern casting; employs 56 karigar.
Jaipur flagship of about 35,000 sq ft: construction complete, interiors underway, timing delayed by artwork.
Delhi Defence Colony showroom to showcase Kundan Polki jewelry; first expansion beyond Rajasthan.

IPO proceeds of INR165 crore: INR65 crore earmarked for debt repayment, which is fully repaid for short-term working capital; about INR30-35 crore used for building or working capital; balance for general corporate purposes.
demand_pricing: Management says festive-season demand was good and wedding-season demand is expected to be strong this year.
Q1 and Q2 described as lighter seasons; bridal demand expected to pick up.
NRI demand for traditional Indian jewelry typically arrives in December; NRI and international B2C not yet a meaningful focus.
Gold price exposure is managed by buying back gold on sale; no exchange hedging. Management says the gold content is not the main value driver of its art-based jewelry.
Management is adding contemporary men's and lightweight jewelry for Gen Z and millennial customers.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the effective tax rate 17-18%, and will it persist?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it falls under a concessional tax regime for manufacturing companies set up around 2019 and that the company remains eligible because it is a manufacturer, with no year-by-year figures given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the inventory composition and inventory days, and what is the post-IPO debt position?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory is INR169 crore, mostly finished goods; management says it is about a year of requirement versus six months of revenue of INR95 crore and does not compute days. The company says it is debt-free after repaying short-term bank debt.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin fall from 29% to 27.8% YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed the decline to higher other expenses, including exhibitions and extensive marketing and business spend ahead of B2C. Management expects the B2C payoff next year.

qa_highlights.question: How much of H1 revenue growth came from gold prices versus volume?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not split revenue into gold price and volume effects, saying the product is art-led and not gold-weight based.

qa_highlights.question: What is the franchise model?
qa_highlights.answer: Delhi is company-owned and major cities will be company-owned; franchising is planned for tier-2 cities, but no discussions have started, and the protocols depend on the city.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company expand into platinum or silver?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it may manufacture platinum if needed and plans international shows, but it has no current sales of these products.

risks_watch: Inventory of INR169 crore is high against revenue; watch inventory turns and working capital after the store launches.
EBITDA margin fell YoY on marketing and exhibition spend; check whether B2C spend converts to revenue next year.
Store timelines have slipped and remain uncertain: Delhi (targeted Q4) and Jaipur flagship (interiors ongoing). Franchise model is undefined.
Concentration and customer data were not disclosed on the call (top-10 B2B share, new wholesale buyers); management said it would respond by email.
Gold price volatility is handled by buying back gold on sales with no exchange hedging; polki and diamond valuation risk.
Tax rate of about 17-18% depends on continued eligibility under the manufacturing concession.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on demand and the brand, but evasive on quantified targets: management repeatedly declined to give growth, margin, or volume numbers, calling forecasts a 'dream'. Answers were sometimes off-topic, and several data requests were deferred to email.
key_quotes: For the 2nd quarter, revenue grew 23.93%, around 24% year on year, to INR59.1 crores.
So from short-term perspective, we are debt-free.
Next year we are planning and we are targeting around 30% of B2C and 70% of B2B, increasing the turnovers the way we, we try to do it.

growth.why: No quantified revenue growth guidance; Q2 revenue grew 23.93% and H1 28.6%, with growth tied to store openings (Delhi Defence Colony targeted Q4, Jaipur delayed) and a 70:30 B2B:B2C mix target for next year, but store timelines and B2C revenue contribution remain unquantified.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA margin fell to 27.8% from about 29% a year ago as marketing and exhibition spend rose ahead of B2C, and management gave no margin target, only saying B2C margins should exceed B2B's next year.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Delhi Defence Colony company-owned store is targeted for Q4 (management said 'by Q4 for sure'), and the 35,000 sq ft Jaipur flagship has construction complete with interiors underway, though timing has slipped on artwork.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Revenue grew 23.93% in Q2 and 28.6% in H1 to INR94.5 crore, with festive and wedding demand described as good, but no volume or growth target was given and the B2C store contribution is expected mainly next year.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Only INR30-35 crore of IPO proceeds is earmarked for building or working capital and no new plant was discussed; the existing Jaipur facility has 400 kg annual installed capacity, and utilisation was not disclosed, so a new capex call is not supported by the call.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management declined to give any quantified growth, margin or volume guidance, calling forecasts a 'dream', so there is no baseline to raise.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Store timelines have already slipped (Jaipur delayed by artwork, Delhi targeted Q4 with uncertain timing) and INR169 crore of inventory, up INR27.7 crore since March, must convert into B2C sales.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management is adding contemporary men's and lightweight jewelry for Gen Z and millennial customers and launching new collections, with the Delhi store showcasing Kundan Polki, but no product launch dates were given.

rows.label: Delhi Defence Colony: first store beyond Rajasthan
rows.why: Company-owned Kundan Polki showroom targeted for Q4, the company's first expansion beyond Rajasthan, though the call was ambiguous on the calendar year.

rows.label: Inventory build ahead of stores
rows.why: Inventory rose INR27.7 crore since March 2026 to INR169 crore (about a year of requirement versus H1 revenue of INR94.5 crore), so working capital could absorb cash until B2C sales convert.

rows.label: Debt-free after IPO repayment
rows.why: Short-term bank debt was repaid from the INR65 crore IPO allocation, and the company says it is now debt-free.
